AIConfiguration.because: Mixed, and not positively self-owned. Its schema carries per-account AI preferences keyed by user_email, but AIConfigurationManager.jsx lists it unfiltered and writes setting_name rows with no user_email at all, so a self predicate would refuse those writes and hide every other account's settings. Falls back to the restrictive default, at the cost of per-account preferences being visible agency-wide.

User.because: D23. Its agency_id, agency_name and account_type are self-editable profile labels — each field's own schema description says so and says never to authorize from it — so no predicate written against this row can decide who may read it. The authority store's membership already models the roster, cannot be edited by its subject, and pennsync_private.context authorizes against it today; caller_roster_ids() asks it. Read only: with no write policy, forced RLS refuses every write from everyone including the record owner, which keeps D23's open profile-write question from quietly resolving itself as allowed.
